- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct — apply downward bias of 3–8% in next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., < -0.2) over 5+ days, model overcorrects downward; adjust forecast upward by 2–5% to avoid underestimation.
- Model frequently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile — reduce first 5–7 days’ forecast by 3–7%.
- Mean reversion bias: if 10+ consecutive days show price decline, model often underestimates rebound — add 2–5% upward bias in next 5–10 days.
- Sentiment reversal (e.g., from +0.3 to -0.2) triggers model lag — delay forecast adjustment by 1–3 days and reduce magnitude of change.
